'''Ikechukwu Somtochukwu Diogu''' {{IPAc-en||audio=Ig-Ikechukwu Somtochukwu Diogu.ogg}} (born September 11, 1983) is a Nigerian-American former professional [[basketball]] player who played six seasons in the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA) and in multiple other leagues in his 18-year career. He was an [[NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]] college player for the [[Arizona State Sun Devils men's basketball|Arizona State Sun Devils]].

==Family and early life==
Diogu's parents, natives of Nigeria, moved to the U.S. in 1980 to pursue further education. They later moved from [[Buffalo, New York]], where he was born in [[Garland, Texas]]. Ike attended [http://www.garlandisdschools.net/page.cfm?p=518 Austin Academy], then enrolled at [[Garland High School]]. Diogu is a member of the [[Igbo people|Igbo ethnic group]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://assets.espn.go.com/ncb/columns/misc/1503226.html |title=Plenty to like about Ike |publisher=ESPN Internet Ventures |first=Curry |last=Kirkpatrick |access-date=January 25, 2009}}</ref>

==College career==
Diogu stands at {{convert|6|ft|9|in}} tall, which is considered slightly undersized for an NBA [[power forward (basketball)|power forward]], but he makes up for his lack of height with his muscle, girth and {{convert|7|ft|4|in}} wingspan.<ref name="nba">{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/playerfile/ike_diogu/bio.html|title=Ike Diogu Stats, Video, Bio, Profile | NBA.com|work=nba.com|access-date=January 26, 2014|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121108195002/http://www.nba.com/playerfile/ike_diogu/bio.html|archive-date=November 8, 2012}}</ref>

Diogu attended [[Arizona State University]], where he excelled on the team under head coach [[Rob Evans (basketball)|Rob Evans]]. He garnered several honors, both in the [[Pac-10 Conference]] and nationally. He won [[Pac-12 Conference Men's Basketball Freshman of the Year|Pac-10 Freshman of the Year]], and then [[Pac-12 Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|Pac-10 Player of the Year]] in his final season with ASU, as a junior. Many speculated that Diogu would enter the draft after playing his third season with Arizona State. On June 21, 2005, he made the decision to enter the NBA draft.

On January 15, 2022, Diogu's number 5 jersey was retired by the Sun Devils. He was the first consensus All-American in program history.<ref>{{cite web| title = Men's Hoops Hosts Colorado Saturday as Ike Diogu No. 5 Goes Into Rafters | work = [[Arizona State Sun Devils]] | date = January 13, 2022 | url = https://thesundevils.com/news/2022/1/13/mens-basketball-mens-hoops-hosts-colorado-saturday-as-ike-diogu-no-5-goes-into-rafters.aspx | access-date = January 17, 2022 }}</ref>

==Professional career==
{{Prose|section|date=January 2023}}
Diogu was selected 9th overall in the first round of the [[2005 NBA draft]] by the [[Golden State Warriors]]. On December 23, 2005, he recorded a professional career-best 27 points on 13–15 shooting, surpassing his previous best by 12 points.<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20170810171052/http://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=251223008 Pistons remain hot with 12-point win over Golden State]</ref> On January 17, 2007, Diogu, whom [[Larry Bird]] called the "gem" of the deal, was traded to the [[Indiana Pacers]] along with teammates [[Mike Dunleavy Jr.]], [[Troy Murphy]], and [[Keith McLeod]] in exchange for [[Stephen Jackson]], [[Al Harrington]], [[Šarūnas Jasikevičius]], and [[Josh Powell]].<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.mopsquad.com/artman2/publish/Indiana_Pacers_72/Pacers_Warriors_announce_8-player_deal.htm |title=Pacers, Warriors announce 8-player deal |agency=Associated Press |date=January 17, 2007 |access-date=December 23, 2007}}</ref>

Following his time in Indiana, Diogu became an NBA journeyman. On June 26, 2008, he was traded to the [[Portland Trail Blazers]] on draft night. He was subsequently moved to the [[Sacramento Kings]] in February 2009 for [[Michael Ruffin]].<ref>[https://www.usatoday.com/sports/basketball/nba/2009-02-18-3352476665_x.htm Blazers get Ruffin from Bulls, send Diogu to Kings]</ref> After brief stints signing with the [[New Orleans Hornets]] and [[Detroit Pistons]], never appearing in a regular-season game for either, he signed with the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] as a free agent in December 2010.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/clippers/news/breakingnews_101222.html |title=CLIPPERS SIGN FREE AGENT FORWARD IKE DIOGU |work=[[NBA.com]] |date=December 22, 2010 |access-date=December 24, 2010}}</ref> While with the Clippers, he scored a season-high 18 points against the Orlando Magic. He later had a one-week stint with the [[San Antonio Spurs]] in January 2012.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/spurs/news/120103_spurs_sign_ike_diogu Spurs Sign Ike Diogu]</ref>

Diogu established a significant international career following his NBA tenure. He joined the [[Xinjiang Flying Tigers]] for the [[2012 CBA Playoffs]] as a replacement for [[Gani Lawal]], before signing with [[Capitanes de Arecibo]] in Puerto Rico.<ref name="sportando">{{cite web|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/world/america/91288/capitanes-de-arecibo-tab-ike-diogu.html|title=Capitanes de Arecibo tab Ike Diogu|work=Sportando.com|date=April 7, 2012|access-date=April 7, 2012}}</ref> Although he attempted NBA comebacks with the [[Phoenix Suns]] and [[New York Knicks]] in 2012 and 2013 respectively,<ref name="azcentral">{{cite web|url=http://www.azcentral.com/members/Blog/PaulCoro/172535|title=Paul Coro's Suns blog | Insiders|publisher=azcentral.com|access-date=January 26, 2014}}</ref><ref>[http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=14355 New York Knicks sign Ike Diogu]</ref> he found success in the [[NBA G League|NBA D-League]] with the [[Bakersfield Jam]]. His performance earned him a spot on the 2014 D-League All-Star roster and the [[NBA G League Impact Player of the Year Award|Impact Player of the Year]] award.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/nba_dleague_all_star_2014_02_03.html Eighth Annual NBA D-League All-Star Game Features 16 Players With NBA Experience] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140207181043/http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/nba_dleague_all_star_2014_02_03.html |date=February 7, 2014 }}</ref><ref>[http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/ike_diogu_nba_dleague_impact_player_2014_04_25.html Jam's Ike Diogu Named 2014 NBA D-League Impact Player of the Year] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140429161056/http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/ike_diogu_nba_dleague_impact_player_2014_04_25.html |date=April 29, 2014 }}</ref> He returned to Puerto Rico in April 2014 to help [[Leones de Ponce (basketball)|Leones de Ponce]] win the league championship.<ref>[http://www.sportando.com/en/world/america/118492/ike-diogu-joins-leones-de-ponce.html Ike Diogu joins Leones de Ponce]</ref>

For several years, Diogu was a fixture in the [[Chinese Basketball Association]]. Between 2014 and 2018, he played for the [[Dongguan Leopards]], returned to the Guangdong Southern Tigers, and replaced injured players for both the [[Jiangsu Monkey King]] and [[Sichuan Blue Whales]].<ref>[http://www.sportando.com/en/world/asia/125851/ike-diogu-signs-with-dongguan-with-nba-out.html Ike Diogu signs with DongGuan with NBA out]</ref><ref>[http://www.sportando.com/en/world/asia/179724/ike-diogu-to-sign-with-guangdong-southern-tigers.html Ike Diogu to sign with Guangdong Southern Tigers]</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Sichuan Whales replace Jamaal Franklin with Ike Diogu|url=https://www.sportando.com/m/en/asia/china/259687/sichuan-whales-replace-jamaal-franklin-with-ike-diogu.html|author=Carchia, E.|website=Sportando.com|date=January 2, 2018}}</ref> In the latter stages of his career, Diogu played globally, joining the [[Shimane Susanoo Magic]] in Japan (2019), [[Chemidor B.C.]] in Iran (2021), and [[Astros de Jalisco]] in Mexico (2021).<ref>[https://www.japantimes.co.jp/sports/2019/08/15/basketball/b-league/former-nba-forward-ike-diogu-joins-susanoo-magic/ Former NBA forward Ike Diogu joins Susanoo Magic] japantimes.co.jp, August 15, 2019</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.notisistema.com/noticias/presentan-a-ike-diogu-y-jorge-gutierrez-como-refuerzos-de-astros-de-jalisco/|title=Presentan a Ike Diogu y Jorge Gutiérrez como refuerzos de Astros de Jalisco|work=Notisistema|first=Martín|last=Navarro Vásquez|date=September 1, 2021|access-date=November 7, 2022|language=es}}</ref> In January 2022, he signed with [[Zamalek SC (basketball)|Zamalek]] of the [[Egyptian Basketball Super League]], making his debut in the [[2022 FIBA Intercontinental Cup]] semifinal.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.afrobasket.com/Egypt/news/726933/Al-Zamalek-inks-Ikechukwu-Diogu|title=Al Zamalek inks Ikechukwu Diogu|last=|first=|date=January 16, 2022|website=afrobasket.com|publisher=|access-date=January 17, 2022}}</ref>

==National team career==
Diogu has played with the senior men's [[Nigeria national basketball team]]. He has competed at two Summer Olympiads: the [[Basketball at the 2012 Summer Olympics – Men|2012]] and [[Basketball at the 2016 Summer Olympics – Men|2016]]. He was named MVP of the 2017 FIBA Afrobasket tournament after averaging 22 points, 8.7 rebounds.<ref>{{cite web| url = http://www.fiba.basketball/afrobasket/2017/Nigeria| title = Nigeria - FIBA Afrobasket 2017 - FIBA.basketball}}</ref>
